subject: Re: RFP request — traffic matrix, degradation signatures and lab evidence
messages:
From: Emily Cho <emily.cho@nebula.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP performance asks — traffic matrix + degradation signatures

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this RFP — Nebula Health is collecting detailed runtime evidence for our procurement review. Two specific asks where we need empirical artifacts: a) a traffic matrix (QPS mix, prompt length distribution, user concurrency profiles) you used for your in-house performance runs; b) "degradation signatures" — i.e., how latency and error modes evolve as load increases (burst, steady ramp, cold starts, region failover).

Can you send sample CSVs and a short methodology that we can attach to the RFP? Key constraints: 8k and 32k context tests, variety of short prompts (10–40 tokens) vs long prompts (1000–4000 tokens), and representative model variants (standard, quantized 4-bit).

Deadline: we'd like artifacts by EOD 28 May to feed procurement and infra.

Thanks — Emily
Procurement | Nebula Health
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Cho <emily.cho@nebula.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP performance asks — traffic matrix + degradation signatures

Hi Emily —

We can provide both. Attached is a traffic_matrix_template.csv and a short methodology_outline.pdf that explains our lab approach, workload synthesis, and fidelity checks. High-level notes:

- We supply both synthetic and replay-based traffic. Synthetic uses a three-bin distribution: short (0–50 tokens): 62%, medium (51–512): 30%, long (513–4k+): 8%. For 32k runs the long bin shifts to 4–6% and we hold more steady-state concurrency for memory pressure tests.
- Degradation signatures are captured across four modes: steady-state ramp, sudden burst (10x QPS for 30s), graceful region failover (traffic shifting across AZs), and cache-warm vs cold-start sweeps.
- We report latencies at p50/p95/p99 and provide QPS where tail shows inflection. We also flag error classes: OOM fallback, transient timeouts (client-level), and model-fallback served by CPU paths.

If that outline looks good I will coordinate a lab run with Marcus and Lauren and send consolidated CSVs and a short summary PDF by 28 May.

Attached: traffic_matrix_template.csv (schema + example)
Attached: methodology_outline.pdf (3 pages)

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Action: NEB-1123 lab run — traffic matrix + degradation capture (28 May)

Team —

Emily at Nebula needs the traffic matrix CSVs and our degradation signatures by EOD 28 May. Please run the following lab matrix and drop artifacts to the shared drive link below. Keep runs reproducible with run ids and seed values. Key test cells: 

1) Models: redwood-mix-v1-7B (float16), redwood-opt-13B (4-bit)
2) Contexts: 8k and 32k (for 13B only we do both)
3) QPS points: baseline (10 QPS), ramp (10->200 QPS over 10m), burst (10 QPS baseline with 30s 100 QPS spike), soak (12h at steady 50 QPS)
4) Prompt mix: use the attached traffic_matrix_template.csv (short/med/long bins + seed).
5) Observability: collect per-token time, model exec time, KV cache hit rates, GPU memory headroom, and error taxonomy.

Deliverables: CSVs (per-run), a 2–3 page degradation signature PDF, and list of any fallback events with cause. Put everything in /shared/NEB-1123/ by 28 May 16:00 PST.

Notes: for 32k context we will toggle quantization and measure encoding time separately — call out encoding as its own column. If you hit persistent OOM on 32k quantized runs, capture the failure fingerprint (GPU logs + coredump stub).

Thanks,
Steph
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 15:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Action: NEB-1123 lab run — traffic matrix + degradation capture (28 May)

Steph — quick summary of runs we completed this morning. Full CSV attached (lab_results_20270525.csv). Highlights and observed degradation signatures: 

Run matrix (summary):
- redwood-mix-v1-7B, 8k context: baseline 50 QPS steady-state; p50=18ms, p95=62ms, p99=145ms; burst to 300 QPS for 30s produced transient p99 spikes to 380ms with 0.02% client timeouts; KV cache hit maintained ~88%
- redwood-opt-13B (4-bit), 8k context: baseline 50 QPS p50=38ms, p95=110ms, p99=260ms; burst 300 QPS spike p99=820ms with 0.12% retries; we observed a model-fallback to CPU path on one node due to a driver memory reclamation event (we captured logs).
- redwood-opt-13B (4-bit), 32k context: baseline 10 QPS p50=210ms, p95=640ms, p99=1.8s; steady ramp to 40 QPS shows p99 inflection near 30 QPS where memory pressure causes KV eviction and tokenization encoding overhead increases; we saw 3 OOM-protected restarts (automated node-recycle) at >35 QPS in this profile.

Degradation signature notes: 
- Two distinct tail modes: (A) CPU/driver induced infra stalls (rare, high-latency spikes across many inferences) and (B) cache-eviction token amplification where prefix cache misses cause near-linear increase in per-token time for long prompts.
- Burst recovery: for 13B 4-bit we saw recovery within 18–35s after a 30s spike, depending on whether KV warmback succeeded.
- Error taxonomy captured in CSV: OOM_RESTART, DRIVER_THROTTLE, CLIENT_TIMEOUT, MODEL_FALLBACK. Each event includes timestamps and node ids.

Attachments: lab_results_20270525.csv (per-request), logs archive reference, run ids. Will add the 12h soak artifacts overnight and produce the short PDF summary by tomorrow morning.

—Marcus
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: RFP performance asks — traffic matrix + degradation signatures (NEB-1123)

Hi Emily —

Thanks for the patience. Attached are the deliverables for NEB-1123: traffic_matrix_template.csv (filled with the seed we used), lab_results_20270525.csv (raw run outputs), and enterprise_degradation_report.pdf (2 pages executive summary + artifact links). Summary highlights below (TL;DR):

- Workloads: synthetic traffic with short/med/long bins (62/30/8%) for 8k; long bin adjusted for 32k runs per your request.
- Representative performance numbers (selected):
  * redwood-mix-v1-7B (8k): baseline 50 QPS — p50=18ms, p95=62ms, p99=145ms
  * redwood-opt-13B (4-bit, 8k): baseline 50 QPS — p50=38ms, p95=110ms, p99=260ms
  * redwood-opt-13B (4-bit, 32k): baseline 10 QPS — p50=210ms, p95=640ms, p99=1.8s; p99 inflection near 30 QPS due to memory pressure
- Degradation signatures captured: cache-eviction token amplification and infrequent infra-driver stalls. We include an event list with timestamps, node ids, and cause classifications.
- Recovery characteristics: typical burst recovery window 18–35s; automated node-recycle reduces persistent OOM exposure but increases tail during the recycle window.

What we provide to you in the Drive link: raw CSVs, per-run logs (node ids redacted on demand), and the concise PDF explaining methodology and key takeaways. If Nebula needs redacted GPU traces or HSM-level telemetry we can coordinate an NDA-scoped artifact package.

Next step: Do you want a short recorded walkthrough (15–20 min) with Marcus to step through the CSVs and call out how to interpret the degradation fingerprints? We can schedule early next week.

Link to artifacts: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/NEB-1123/traffic-matrix
PDF report: https://s3.redwood-inference.com/runs/NEB-1123/report-20270528.pdf

Best regards,
